title: Backing up a single profile email account and exclude other profiles.
creator: JJM
content:
Current official docs explains how to backup and move your profile, it assumes you only have one. I have multiple profiles which means about a 20GB backup but I only want to backup one specific profile (<2GB).

The backup is not for recovery but I need to keep a history records for a specific account which can be accessed through Thunderbird even if the original email account no longer exists.

To backup/copy its recommended to do it for this folder %APPDATA%\Thunderbird\Profiles\ (about 20 GB)

While all I need is %APPDATA\Thunderbird\Profiles\xxxxx.default-release\ImapMail\Important_stuff* (2 GB folder and .msf file)

Any better solutions than these?

  1. Use a backup method that excludes specific folder and files in backup/copy of
  2. Have a completely different installation of Thunderbird that only does the Important_stuff account (Thunderbird portable looks like it might do the job).

I suspect the first version will pick up a lot of unnecessary configuration and other stuff.

title: Repeated "Authentication Failure" trying to connect to outlook.live.com servers using IMAP.
creator: alex.farlie
content:
Program : Thunderbird Build - 115.18.0 esr .

How to reproduce:

Log into outlook.live.com an ensure IMAP is enabled.

Start Thunderbird and create a new 'mail' account manually, given the account settings provided by outlook.live.com. (https://support.microsoft.com/en-gb/outlook/pop-imap-and-smtp-settings-for-outlook-com)

The account may have to be setup manually.

Also you may have to setup the outgoing SMTP server to use OAuth2 manually as an SMTP server directly, as the normal dialog presented during manual setup did not provide this option unless the servers were set up indvidually.

The e-mail account details should be set up.

What should have happened:

SMTP server should have permitted Ouath2 authentication during setup. Thunderbird should have presented a login to obtain a password, and retrieved messages to a local inbox.

What actually happened: "Authentication failure when connecting to server outlook.office365.com"

Possible causes :

  • Build not actually supporting Oauth2 despite claiming to.
  • Third party server is claiming to support IMAP/Oauth2 but refuses to recognise credentials sent by Thunderbird.
  • Build too old.

Thank you.
